title: Battery Safe
brief: Returns whether the drone's battery percentage is high enough to fly.
description: Camp rule: a drone may only take off if its battery is at 20 percent or higher. Write a function that takes the battery percentage as a number and returns True if it is safe to fly, and False otherwise.
solution:
def battery_safe(battery):
    return battery >= 20
hints: Think about which comparison operator means 'at least'.
battery >= 20 is True right at the boundary.
explainer: Since the rule says 20 or higher counts as safe, the comparison uses >= so that exactly 20 is still True.

title: Altitude Legal
brief: Returns whether an altitude in feet is within the camp's legal flying range.
description: At camp, drones must fly no lower than the ground (0 feet) and no higher than 120 feet. Write a function that takes an altitude and returns True if it is within that legal range (0 and 120 both count as legal), and False otherwise.
solution:
def altitude_legal(altitude):
    return 0 <= altitude <= 120
hints: You need two comparisons joined together, or a chained comparison.
0 and 120 themselves should count as legal.
explainer: The chained comparison 0 <= altitude <= 120 checks both edges of the range at once, including the boundaries.

title: Seconds To Minutes
brief: Converts a flight time given in seconds into whole minutes.
description: A flight log records time in seconds, but campers want to know whole minutes flown. Write a function that takes the number of seconds and returns how many whole minutes that is, dropping any leftover seconds.
solution:
def seconds_to_minutes(seconds):
    return seconds // 60
hints: Which operator divides and throws away the remainder?
60 seconds make one minute.
explainer: Integer division with // gives the number of whole minutes and automatically discards the leftover seconds.

title: Signal Lost
brief: Returns whether the drone's remote control signal has been lost.
description: A drone's controller reports a signal strength in bars, where 0 or fewer bars means the signal is lost. Write a function that takes the bar count and returns True if the signal is lost, and False if there is still some signal.
solution:
def signal_lost(bars):
    return bars <= 0
hints: Signal is lost at 0 bars or below.
Use <= so 0 itself counts as lost.
explainer: The comparison bars <= 0 covers both exactly zero bars and any negative reading, both meaning the signal is gone.

title: Cleared For Launch
brief: Returns whether a drone is cleared to take off based on battery and wind conditions.
description: Before launch, a drone needs at least 15 percent battery AND the wind must be calm. Write a function that takes the battery percentage and a boolean for whether the wind is calm, and returns True only when both conditions are met.
solution:
def cleared_for_launch(battery, wind_calm):
    return battery >= 15 and wind_calm
hints: Both conditions must be true at the same time.
Combine a comparison with the wind_calm boolean using 'and'.
explainer: The and operator only returns True when both the battery check and wind_calm are True, matching the two-condition rule.

title: Temp Safe
brief: Returns whether the outside temperature is safe for the drone's motors to operate.
description: Drone motors at camp are only rated to fly between -10 and 40 degrees Celsius, inclusive. Write a function that takes the temperature and returns True if it is within that safe range, and False otherwise.
solution:
def temp_safe(temp):
    return -10 <= temp <= 40
hints: Two boundaries need checking, one on each side of zero.
Both -10 and 40 should count as safe.
explainer: The chained comparison -10 <= temp <= 40 tests both the low and high boundary in one line, including the endpoints.

title: Count Turns
brief: Counts how many turning commands appear in a flight route.
description: A route is a list of single-letter command strings such as "F" (forward), "B" (backward), "L" (turn left), "R" (turn right), "U" (up), and "D" (down). Write a function that takes a route and returns how many of the commands are turns, meaning "L" or "R".
solution:
def count_turns(route):
    return sum(1 for c in route if c == "L" or c == "R")
hints: Loop through the route and check each command against both turn letters.
Only 'L' and 'R' count; everything else is ignored.
explainer: The function walks through every command and adds one to the count whenever it matches 'L' or 'R', ignoring all other commands.

title: Remove Unsafe
brief: Returns a copy of a route with every occurrence of one unsafe command taken out.
description: Sometimes a command gets flagged as unsafe and every copy of it must be stripped from the route before flying. Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings) and an unsafe command string, and returns a new list containing every command from the route except the unsafe one, keeping the original order. The original route list must not be changed.
solution:
def remove_unsafe(route, command):
    return [c for c in route if c != command]
hints: Build a brand new list rather than editing the one you were given.
Keep everything that does NOT equal the unsafe command.
explainer: A list comprehension builds a fresh list, keeping every command that isn't equal to the unsafe one, so the original list passed in is never modified.

title: Adjacent Repeat
brief: Checks whether a route repeats the same command twice in a row anywhere.
description: Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings) and returns True if any two commands next to each other in the list are exactly the same, and False if no two neighbors ever match. A route with fewer than two commands can never have a repeat, so it returns False.
hints: Compare each command to the one right after it.
Stop and return True as soon as you find a match.
explainer: The loop checks every pair of neighboring commands and returns True the moment two in a row match; if the loop finishes with no match, it returns False.

title: Same Start End
brief: Checks whether a route's first and last commands are the same.
description: Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings) and returns True if the first command in the list is exactly the same as the last command, and False otherwise. An empty route has no first or last command, so it should return False.
hints: Check the length first so you don't crash on an empty list.
Index 0 is the first command and -1 is the last.
explainer: The function first guards against an empty list, then compares the item at index 0 with the item at index -1, which is always the last element.

title: Commands To Word
brief: Joins a list of one-letter drone commands into a single command string.
description: Some drones accept a whole route as one string instead of a list. Write a function that takes a route (a list of single-letter command strings) and returns a single string made by joining all the letters together in order, with nothing in between them.
solution:
def commands_to_word(route):
    return "".join(route)
hints: There's a string method that joins a list of strings together.
Use an empty string as the separator.
explainer: The empty string's join method glues every element of the list together back to back, with no separator between them.

title: Count SOS
brief: Counts how many times an SOS distress signal appears in a radio log.
description: A drone's radio log is one long string of text. Write a function that takes the log string and returns how many times the exact text "SOS" appears in it. Overlapping matches should not be double counted.
solution:
def count_sos(message):
    return message.count("SOS")
hints: There's a string method built for counting how many times something appears.
It already avoids double-counting overlaps.
explainer: The str.count method scans the string and returns the number of non-overlapping times the substring "SOS" occurs.

title: Trim Ends
brief: Removes the first and last command from a route, unless the route is too short.
description: Sometimes the first and last commands of a route are just takeoff and landing and campers want to see only the middle. Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings). If the route has more than 2 commands, return a new list with the first and last commands removed. If it has 2 or fewer commands, return an empty list instead.
hints: Slicing with [1:-1] skips the first and last item.
Check the length before slicing to handle the short-route case.
explainer: When the route is longer than 2 commands, the slice route[1:-1] grabs everything except the first and last item; otherwise the function returns an empty list.

title: Landing Report
brief: Builds a short landing status message for a drone.
description: After every flight, campers print a status message. Write a function that takes the drone's name and a boolean for whether the landing was safe, and returns a string. If safe is True, return the drone's name followed by " has landed safely.". If safe is False, return the drone's name followed by " needs help!".
hints: Branch on the safe boolean with an if/else.
Use + to glue the name onto the front of each message.
explainer: The function checks the safe flag and glues the drone's name onto whichever of the two fixed messages matches.

title: Total Altitude Gain
brief: Adds up a list of altitude changes to find the drone's total altitude change.
description: A flight log lists altitude changes in feet for each step of a flight, where positive numbers mean climbing and negative numbers mean descending. Write a function that takes this list and returns the total altitude change by adding every number together.
solution:
def total_altitude_gain(moves):
    return sum(moves)
hints: Python has a built-in function that adds up all the numbers in a list.
An empty list of moves should add up to 0.
explainer: The built-in sum function adds every number in the moves list together to get the overall altitude change.

title: Net Displacement
brief: Adds up a list of movement steps to find the drone's total displacement.
description: A drone's flight is recorded as a list of moves, where each move is a two-number list [dx, dy] describing how far it shifted sideways (dx) and forward or back (dy) during that step. Write a function that takes this list of moves and returns a single [dx, dy] list giving the drone's total displacement, found by adding up all the dx values and all the dy values separately.
solution:
def net_displacement(moves):
    dx = sum(m[0] for m in moves)
    dy = sum(m[1] for m in moves)
    return [dx, dy]
hints: Track two running totals, one for dx and one for dy.
Each move is itself a two-item list, so m[0] is dx and m[1] is dy.
explainer: The function separately sums every move's dx and every move's dy, then packages the two running totals as the final [dx, dy] result.

title: Longest Straight Run
brief: Finds the length of the longest stretch of identical commands in a row.
description: Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings) and returns the length of the longest run of the exact same command repeated back to back. For example, ["F", "F", "F", "L", "F"] has a run of three F's in a row, which is the longest. An empty route has a longest run of 0.
hints: Keep a running counter of the current streak, and a separate 'best so far' counter.
Reset the current streak back to 1 whenever the command changes.
explainer: The loop walks through the route keeping a running streak counter that grows while commands repeat and resets to 1 when they change, while best always remembers the largest streak seen.

title: Battery Death Index
brief: Simulates battery drain across a list of commands and reports which command kills the battery.
description: Each command in a route costs some battery to run. Write a function that takes a list of battery costs (one number per command, in order) and a starting battery amount, then simulates running the commands one at a time, subtracting each cost from the battery. Return the index of the command during which the battery first drops to 0 or below. If the battery survives every command in the list, return -1.
hints: Keep a running battery total that you update inside the loop.
Check the battery right after each subtraction, and remember the loop's index when it fails.
explainer: The function subtracts each cost from a running battery total in order, and returns the loop index as soon as the total drops to 0 or below; if it never does, it returns -1.

title: Max Altitude
brief: Simulates a flight's altitude changes and reports the highest point reached.
description: A drone starts a flight at altitude 0. Write a function that takes a list of altitude changes (positive for climbing, negative for descending) and simulates applying them one at a time. Return the highest altitude the drone reaches at any point during the flight, including the starting altitude of 0 if the drone never climbs above it.
hints: Track the current altitude as a running total that changes with each move.
Keep a separate 'best so far' that only updates when the current altitude beats it, and start both at 0.
explainer: The function keeps a running altitude total updated by each move and a best tracker that only grows when the running total sets a new high, starting both at ground level 0.

title: Drop Count
concept: Loops: comparing to the previous value
brief: Counts how many times a battery reading drops compared to the reading right before it.
description: A drone logs its battery percentage every few seconds into a list. Write a function that takes this list of readings and returns how many times a reading is lower than the reading that came directly before it. The very first reading has nothing before it, so it never counts as a drop.
hints: Start comparing from the second reading onward.
Compare each reading only to the one immediately before it, not to the very first reading.
explainer: The loop starts at index 1 and compares each reading to its immediate predecessor, adding one to the count every time the battery went down since the last reading.

title: Farthest Point
concept: Loops: tracking position along a line
brief: Simulates forward and backward moves along a line and finds the farthest distance reached from the start.
description: A drone flies back and forth along a straight line, starting at position 0. Write a function that takes a list of moves, where a positive number means moving forward that many meters and a negative number means moving backward that many meters. Simulate the flight and return the greatest distance from the starting point reached at any moment, no matter which direction it was in.
hints: Track the drone's current position as a running total.
Use abs() to compare distance in either direction, and keep the largest one seen.
explainer: The function keeps a running position updated by each move, and remembers the largest absolute distance from 0 that position ever reaches during the simulation.

title: Safe Landing
concept: Loops: checking a running value against limits
brief: Simulates a flight's altitude and checks whether it ever goes below the ground or above a ceiling.
description: A drone starts on the ground at altitude 0. Write a function that takes a list of altitude changes and a ceiling height, and simulates the flight step by step. Return True only if the altitude stays between 0 (the ground) and the ceiling (inclusive) at every single moment of the flight, starting from before the first move. Return False if it ever dips below the ground or climbs above the ceiling.
hints: Check the altitude after every single move, not just at the end.
Return False the instant the altitude breaks a limit; stop simulating early.
explainer: The function updates a running altitude after every move and immediately returns False the moment that altitude goes below 0 or above the ceiling, only returning True if the whole flight stays in range.

title: Final Heading
brief: Simulates a series of turns and returns the drone's final compass heading.
description: A drone starts facing heading 0 degrees. Write a function that takes a route (a list of command strings) and simulates it: each "L" turns the drone 90 degrees to the left (subtract 90), each "R" turns it 90 degrees to the right (add 90), and any other command does not change the heading. Return the drone's final heading as a number from 0 up to but not including 360, wrapping around if it goes negative or past 360.
hints: Add or subtract 90 for each turn command as you loop through the route.
The % (modulo) operator wraps a number back into the 0-359 range, even from a negative number.
explainer: The loop accumulates a running heading by adding or subtracting 90 for each turn, and the final % 360 wraps the result into the 0-359 range even if it went negative.

title: Sudden Drop Index
brief: Finds the first place in a battery log where the level suddenly plunges by a large amount.
description: A drone logs its battery percentage over time into a list. Write a function that takes this list of readings and a drop amount, and returns the index of the first reading where the battery fell by at least that drop amount compared to the immediately previous reading. If no such sudden drop ever happens, return -1.
hints: Compare each reading to the one right before it, starting at index 1.
The drop size is the previous reading minus the current one.
explainer: The loop checks, for each reading starting at index 1, whether the previous reading minus the current one meets or beats the drop amount, returning the first index where that happens.
